title.narrative: Building Climate Resilience in the Pyanj River Basin

description.narrative:
The project aims to increase resilience to climate vulnerability and change of communities in the Pyanj River Basin. The project's impact will be improved livelihoods of Pyanj River Basin communities vulnerable to climate variability and change. The project's outcome will be reduced adverse effects of climate variability and climate change in 59 villages in 19 jamoats in the Pyanj River Basin. The project has four outputs:
Output 1 is flood protection infrastructure climate-proofed in 10 jamoats. It will (i) upgrade and climate-proof flood and mudflow protection infrastructure in 10 locations, including riverbank reinforcement, embankment reconstruction, restoration of stream beds, terracing and planting of trees, and soil stabilization; (ii) establish O&M practices, develop O&M guidelines, and train local units of the responsible agencies; (iii) develop early warning communication systems through the use of modern technologies; (iv) establish disaster risk management committees; and (v) conduct training and disseminate information on the impact of climate change and adaptation measures for local government officials and local institutions such as khashar (mutual self-help groups), mahala (neighborhood associations), and women's committees.
Output 2 is irrigation systems climate-proofed in eight jamoats. It will (i) rehabilitate and climate-proof irrigation canals and network assets, including reconstruction and desilting of drainage and delivery channels and rehabilitation of pumping stations; (ii) pilot a drip irrigation scheme; (iii) strengthen water users' associations; and (iv) provide advice and disseminate information on water resources management and climate-resilient agricultural practices to farmers, local government officials, women' groups, and other stakeholders.
Output 3 is water supply infrastructure climate-proofed in seven jamoats. It will (i) rehabilitate and climate-proof seven rural drinking water supply systems, including rehabilitation, upgrade, and construction of boreholes, provision of new and rehabilitated pumping equipment, and construction of new service reservoirs and water tanks; (ii) establish O&M practices for drinking water supply systems, develop O&M guidelines, and train local units of the responsible agencies; (iii) establish drinking water consumer groups to influence responsible agencies and ensure performance of the water supply facilities; and (iv) raise awareness of health and other risks associated with climate change.
Output 4 is micro credits and micro deposits made available to promote climate resilience in the Pyanj River Basin. It will (i) expand capacity of participating financial institutions (PFIs) in the Pyanj River Basin to accept micro and small deposits and provide micro loans in support of climate-resilient economic activities; (ii) provide credit lines for agricultural improvements (climate-resilient agriculture credit line) and economic diversification (income diversification credit line), particularly targeting women; (iii) strengthen financial literacy of the local population; and (iv) assess the feasibility of collateral insurance linked to credit and, if appropriate, pilot a credit insurance scheme.
The project will:
- Protect at least 231 hectares of arable land from annual floods and 1,490 hectares of arable land from high floods by 2019. Training on disaster risk management will be provided to communities. Disaster risk management groups will be established and early warning systems developed to support communities in their responses to floods;
- Service 1,450 hectares of arable land with irrigation water. Water user's associations (WUAs) will be established and trained to deliver agricultural advice. Women will represent at least 20% of the WUAs members. Training on climate-resilient agriculture practices will be provided to farmers, local government officials, women' groups, and other stakeholders. A drip irrigation scheme will be piloted;
- Service at least 4,150 households with water supply. Drinking water consumer groups will be established to influence responsible agencies and ensure performance of the water supply facilities. Women will represent at least 30% of members of water consumer groups. Information on health and other risks associated with climate change will be disseminated to local communities;
- Make available micro credits and micro deposits to at least 1,000 households to promote climate resilience agriculture and economic diversification in the Pyanj River Basin. A third of all subloans will be for either women or enterprises with a minimum of 50% ownership by women. Training on financial literacy will be provided to local population. The feasibility of collateral insurance linked to credit will be assessed and, if appropriate, a credit insurance scheme will be piloted in the river basin.
The project will have three executing agencies: (i) the Ministry of Land Reclamation and Water Resources (MLRWR), (ii) the State Unitary Enterprise for Housing and Communal Services (Khochagii Manziliyu Kommunali - KMK), and (iii) the MOF. MLRWR will be responsible for outputs 1 and 2, KMK will be responsible for output 3, and MOF will be responsible for output 4. Overall coordination will be provided by the Executive Office of the President and the Pilot Program for Climate Resilience Interministerial Committee, which is chaired by the deputy prime minister. A project steering group comprising the three executing agencies will provide implementation guidance and monitor project performance. The project management structure will consist of (i) a project management office (PMO) in the MLRWR and four project implementation offices (PIOs) in the Pyanj river basin; (ii) the existing project implementation group in the KMK and three PIOs; and (iii) the PMO in the MOF, which is jointly financed under three ADB projects. The project management units will ensure compliance with grant covenants, project administration manual, gender action plan, and financial and safeguard requirements. Specific responsibilities will include (i) overall financial management; (ii) procurement, disbursement, and accounting; and (iii) monitoring and evaluation, including progress reports for submission to ADB.
Tajikistan-regulated microfinance institutions (MFIs) may apply to be a PFI if they meet the following eligibility criteria: (i) compliance with mandatory prudential standards regulation in Tajikistan; (ii) corporate, financial, management, and governance practices acceptable to ADB and MOF, and satisfactory completion of ADB's integrity, anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism due diligence requirements; (iii) successful experience in the rural development sector; and (iv) willingness and ability to grow and service beneficiaries in the Pyanj River Basin in line with the objectives of the project, including the ability to offer deposits. Microfinance institutions will be required to (i) submit audited financial statements for the 2 years prior to entering into a subsidiary loan agreement, (ii) implement a basic environment and social management system, and (iii) implement adequate anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism customer due diligence measures. PFIs will enter into a subsidiary loan agreement with the MOF and a project agreement with ADB. ADB conducted financial and integrity due diligence on four microfinance institutions from July 2012 to March 2013. Based on the results of the due diligence assessment, IMON International and OXUS have been selected to participate in the first round of microfinance activities. Half of the total funds ($1.4 million) will be allocated to IMON International and OXUS in equal amounts. The remaining total funds will be allocated by MOF, subject to ADB concurrence, to selected and eligible MFIs.
The project was approved by the ADB board on 25 July 2013. A grant agreement was signed between ADB and Republic of Tajikistan on 18 September 2013.

description.narrative: Adverse effects of climate variability and climate change reduced in 59 villages in 19 Jamoats in the Pyanj River Basin

At least 50% of surveyed beneficiaries confirm improved access to financial resources for climate change adaptation. Achievement: 50 Progress/Status: Achieved. More than 50% of surveyed beneficiaries confirmed improved access to financial resources Data Source: Public opinion survey carried out by the Project

At least 50% of surveyed women beneficiaries confirm improved access to financial resources for climate change adaptation. Achievement: 50 Progress/Status: Achieved. More than 50% of surveyed women confirmed improved access to financial resources Data Source: Public opinion survey carried out by the Project

Economic losses from floods reduced by 20% (baseline = $ 80 million in 2011 nationally) Achievement: 4000000 Progress/Status: Achieved. From 2015 to 2020, the Province of Khatlon reported 36 natural disasters in the project area, which caused economic losses of $11.5 million and 6 deaths. No figures were made available for GBAO. Flood control infrastructure was commissioned in 2017-2018 (varying by village). From 2015 to 2020 total reported losses dropped by approximately 80.0%. These positive developments may be due in part to the project intervention; however, they may also be attributable in part to selection bias (i.e., not showing years prior to 2015) and to natural weather cycles (i.e., a statistical anomaly). Data Source: Statistics and reports of Ministry of Health and other statistics.
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Flood protection infrastructure is climate proofed in 10 jamoats Indicator: At least 1,490 ha of arable land protected from high floods (frequency over 1 in 10 years but less than 1 in 50 years) (2012 baseline=0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. 3,973.5 ha of arable land were protected from annual floods, including the high flood in 2017. The flood protection infrastructure rehabilitation works completed in 10 districts. Bank protection works were completed at a length of 16.72 km, and work was carried out to clean riverbeds of 8.04-km long. 950 trees for protection of villages from mudflows were planted. Data Source: Statistics of Committee for Emergency Situations and MWRLR

Output: Flood protection infrastructure is climate proofed in 10 jamoats Indicator: At least 231 ha or arable land protected from annual floods (frequency less than 1 in 10 years) (2012 baseline=0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. 3,973.5 ha of arable land were protected from annual floods, including the high flood in 2017. The flood protection infrastructure rehabilitation works completed in 10 districts. Bank protection works were completed at a length of 16.72 km, and work was carried out to clean riverbeds of 8.04-km long. 950 trees for protection of villages from mudflows were planted. Data Source: Report of the monitoring program established under PPCR

Output: Flood protection infrastructure is climate proofed in 10 jamoats Indicator: At least 500 people trained on disaster risk management by the DRMCs in 10 jamoats Achievement: 63 Progress/Status: Achieved. DRMCs were created in 17 jamoats in 10 districts. 563 people, including 333 women, which comprise 59%, were trained on disaster risk management by the DRMCs. 233 of the 465 members of the DMRCs were women (50%). Data Source: End of project surveys with head of target jamoats

Output: Flood protection infrastructure is climate proofed in 10 jamoats Indicator: Disaster risk management plans based on early warning system established in 10 target jamoats by 2017 Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: Achieved. DRM plans were developed in 10 districts as planned. Data Source: Report of the monitoring program established under PPCR

Output: Irrigation systems are climate-proofed in 8 Jamoats Indicator: At least 1450 ha of arable land serviced by 5 climate proofed irrigation canals and network (2012 baseline=0) Achievement: 520 Progress/Status: Achieved. 2,081 ha of arable land serviced by 5 climate-proofed irrigation canals and network. The irrigation infrastructure rehabilitation works completed in 8 districts, include (i) 19.04-km length of drainage collectors and canals cleaned, (ii) 6.12-km length of irrigation system restored, (iii) 3 pumping stations repaired, and (iv) a drip irrigation scheme piloted. Data Source: Cadaster of agricultural land use in the communities of the Pyanj River Basin

Output: Irrigation systems are climate-proofed in 8 Jamoats Indicator: At least 20% of members of WUAs are women Achievement: 53 Progress/Status: Achieved. In 2016, the NGO “Umedbakhsh”, based on the Project plan, established 5 WUAs in 3 pilot districts. In total, 1,538 people were members of WUAs, of which 820 (53%) were women. Data Source: Monitoring program established under PPCR

Output: Irrigation systems are climate-proofed in 8 Jamoats Indicator: At least 200 farmers trained on climate-resilient agriculture practices by 8 WUAs Achievement: 200 Progress/Status: Achieved. 200 farmers were trained, of whom 40 (20%) were women. Data Source: Monitoring program established under PPCR

Output: Irrigation systems are climate-proofed in 8 Jamoats Indicator: At least 8 WUAs trained to deliver agricultural advice Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Achieved. Five newly established WUAs and three existing WUAs were trained to deliver agricultural advice. Data Source: End-of-project survey with heads of 8 jamoats

Output: Micro-credit and microdeposit established to promote climate resilience Indicator: $2.8 million of ADB grant fund is used for onlending to beneficiaries Achievement: 000 Progress/Status: Achieved. Project financial statements supplied by the three PFIs showed full disbursement of $2.8 million from the ADB grant. Data Source: Quarterly reports from PFIs and MFIs

Output: Micro-credit and microdeposit established to promote climate resilience Indicator: 3 branches of finance institutions offer climate resilience micro credits Achievement: 6 Progress/Status: Achieved. PFIs opened 18 branches in the project region by 2019. Data Source: End of project surveys on access to financial services

Output: Micro-credit and microdeposit established to promote climate resilience Indicator: A minimum of 30% of all subloans are to eligible subborrowers who are either women or enterprises with a minimum of 50% ownership by women Achievement: 31 Progress/Status: Achieved. Measured in $ terms, $2,824,000 was disbursed, out of this $0,86 mln, i.e. 31% of subloan volume, was extended to women or to enterprises with a minimum of 50% ownership by women by 2019. Data Source: Quarterly reports from PFIs and MFIs

Output: Micro-credit and microdeposit established to promote climate resilience Indicator: At least 1,000 people access climate resilient agriculture and revenue diversification credit lines Achievement: 934 Progress/Status: Achieved. 1,934 people received loans. Data Source: Number of signed subsidiary loans agreements signed by PFIs for credit lines

Output: Micro-credit and microdeposit established to promote climate resilience Indicator: At least 1,000 potential borrowers, of whom at least 50% are women, are trained in climate-resilient agricultural practice by 2018 Achievement: 1537 Progress/Status: Achieved. A total of 68 training sessions were conducted which covered 1,607 trainees from the potential borrowers, out of whom 820 or 51% were women. Data Source: Attendance sheets and evaluation forms from training courses

Output: Water supply infrastructure is climate-proofed in 7 Jamoats Indicator: At least 30% of members of Water Consumer Groups are women Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: Partially achieved. In total 2825 people were mobilized in water consumer groups (WCG), 582 of whom are women, which is 20% of the total number of WCG's members. Of the 117 officers of the water consumer groups 33 (30%) were women. Data Source: Monitoring program established under PPCR

Output: Water supply infrastructure is climate-proofed in 7 Jamoats Indicator: At least 350 people trained on climate change risks by the Water Consumer Groups in 7 jamoats Achievement: 118 Progress/Status: Achieved. Of the 368 trainees, 146 (39.7%) were women. Data Source: Monitoring program established under PPCR

Output: Water supply infrastructure is climate-proofed in 7 Jamoats Indicator: At least 4,150 households serviced by 7 climate proofed water supply systems Achievement: 500 Progress/Status: Achieved. An estimated 4,500 households in 15 villages in 5 districts received improved water supply. The water supply infrastructure works completed in 7 districts include (i) 10 boreholes drilled, 5 boreholes rehabilitated (ii) 10 reservoirs built, (iii) 2 water tanks installed, (iv) 6 pumping equipment installed, (v) 58.13-km water pipes installed, (vi) 2,660 water meters installed, (vii) 5 chlorination buildings constructed. Data Source: Monitoring program established under PPCR

Output: Water supply infrastructure is climate-proofed in 7 Jamoats Indicator: At least 50% of surveyed beneficiaries confirm perception of improved access to drinking water Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Achieved. In the closing survey, 4,610 people were interviewed, of which 2,212 (48%) were women. 100% of respondents said access to water was adequate compared with just 6% in 2016.100% of respondents reported that water quality is excellent now, compared with just 30% in the baseline survey. Data Source: End-of-project surveys with heads of target communities
